title: Get a faster decision on your visa, settlement or citizenship application
description: Getting a faster decision on a visa, settlement or citizenship application; priority service, super priority service; waiting times; how to check if you're eligible
text:
# Get a faster decision on your visa, settlement or citizenship application

## Applying for a faster decision

You may be able to pay for a faster decision on a visa, settlement ('indefinite leave to remain') or citizenship application.

Using the 'priority service' means you'll usually get a decision within:

- 5 working days for most visa and settlement applications

- 30 working days for Family visa applications from outside the UK and citizenship applications

Using the 'super priority service' for visa and settlement applications means you'll usually get a decision by the end of the next working day. You cannot use the 'super priority service' for citizenship applications.

Your processing time ends when you get a letter or email telling you that a decision has been made.

It can take longer to get a decision - for example, if the Home Office needs to ask you for more information or check your details with other government departments. You'll be told if this is the case.

If the decision takes longer, you will not usually get your money back. Find out about getting a refund of your priority service fee.

If you're in the UK:

- you must have permission to be here to apply for the priority or super priority service

- you can only pay for a faster decision on certain visas

## Using the priority service

If you're eligible you can choose the 'priority service' when you apply. You'll need to pay £500 in addition to the application fee.

Using the 'priority service' means you'll usually get a decision within 5 working days, or 30 working days for citizenship applications.

Using the priority service usually takes up to 30 working days for Family visa applications from outside the UK if you're applying as a:

- partner or spouse

- parent

- child

- adult coming to be cared for by a relative

The time starts from either:

- the day of your appointment, if you prove your identity in person

- the working day after you finished uploading your documents, if you use the 'UK Immigration: ID Check' app

It can take longer to get a decision - for example, if the Home Office needs to ask you for more information.

You'll be told whether you can prove your identity in person or using the app when you apply.

## Using the super priority service

If you're eligible you can choose the 'super priority service' when you apply. You'll need to pay £1,000 in addition to the application fee.

How quickly you get a decision depends on when you prove your identity.

You cannot use the super priority service for citizenship applications.

### If you prove your identity in person

You'll usually get a decision:

- by the end of the next working day after your appointment, if your appointment is on a weekday

- 2 working days after your appointment, if your appointment is at the weekend or on a bank holiday

It can take longer - for example, if the Home Office needs to ask you for more information or check your details with other government departments. You'll be told if this is the case.

### If you use the 'UK Immigration: ID Check' app

You'll usually get a decision:

- by the end of the next working day if you finish uploading your documents on a weekday

- 2 working days after you finish uploading your documents if you upload them on a weekend or a bank holiday

It can take longer - for example, if the Home Office needs to ask you for more information or check your details with other government departments. You'll be told if this is the case.

## Applying with family members for visa or settlement applications

For each family member applying with you, you'll need to pay an additional:

-
£500, to get a decision within 5 working days

-
£1,000, to get a decision by the end of the next working day

Every family member will need to pay for a faster decision. You'll get a decision for everyone at the same time.

If any of your family members need to have their fingerprints and photograph taken in person, a decision may take longer.

## After you've applied

You'll get a letter or email telling you the Home Office has made a decision on your application. It will tell you what you need to do next.

Check your email's spam folder if you're having problems getting messages from the Home Office.

### When you might wait longer for a decision

You might wait longer for a decision if the Home Office needs to check your details with other government departments or asks you for more information. You'll be told if they need to do this.

If you need to provide more information, you'll be told how and when to provide it. When this has been received, your application will be prioritised.

## Eligible visas when applying from inside the UK

You can apply for a faster decision on certain:

- visa applications

- applications to extend your stay in the UK

- applications to settle in the UK

These tables list the eligible applications and whether you can pay to get a faster decision:

- within 5 working days

- by the end of the next working day

They also list the visa applications eligible for getting a faster decision depending on whether you're applying:

- as the main applicant

- as a dependent partner or child

There's a limit on how many people can apply for a faster decision. If you're not offered the option to apply for a faster decision, you can still complete a standard application.

Whether you can get a faster decision depends on what you're applying for and how you prove your identity.

You'll prove your identity by either:

- attending an appointment at a UK Visa and Citizen Application Services (UKVCAS) centre

- using the 'UK Immigration: ID Check' app to scan your identity document

You'll find out if you can get a faster decision and what you need to do when you apply.

## Eligible types of citizenship applications

You can use the priority service if you're applying online for British citizenship:

- by naturalisation

- if you're registering a child under 18

- as a British Overseas Territories citizen, British Overseas citizen, British subject, British protected person or British National (Overseas)

- if you were born on or after 1 January 1983 and lived in the UK up to the age of 10

- if you're becoming a British citizen again after giving it up ('renouncing' it)

- if you were born to a British father and your parents were not married

- if you were born before 1 January 1983 to a British mother

- if you're a stateless person

You'll be told if you're eligible for the priority service when you're applying.

You cannot apply for the priority service using a paper form.

## Getting a refund of your priority or super priority fee

The rules for getting a refund depend on whether you're cancelling your visa application or not, and what stage your application is at.

If your application is refused, you will not get a refund.

## If you're cancelling your visa application

You may get a refund of the priority service fee if you cancel your visa application. It depends on how you were told to prove your identity and whether or not you have already given your fingerprints and photo (biometric information).

### If you were told to prove your identity in person

You will get a refund if you have not given your fingerprints and photo.

You will not usually get a refund if you have already given your fingerprints and photo.

The refund will not always be paid automatically - you may need to ask for a refund.

### If you used the 'UK Immigration: ID Check' app to prove your identity

You will get a refund if both of the following apply:

- you cancelled your application before the deadline you were given for uploading your evidence

- you have not selected 'confirm and upload' in the app - either to upload your evidence or confirm you do not have anything to upload

The refund will not always be paid automatically - you may need to ask for a refund.

## If you are not cancelling your visa application

You will not usually get a refund of the priority service fee if you are not cancelling your visa application. Each case is considered individually.

You will not get a refund if you do not get a decision in time because the Home Office needed more information or evidence to make the decision.

The Home Office may give you a refund if they could not give you a decision in time because of something outside their control, for example a technical problem.

## How to get a refund

You'll automatically get a refund when you cancel your visa application if you have not given your biometric information and you're either:

- in the UK

- outside the UK and you paid the priority service fee at the same time as you paid your visa application fee

Otherwise, you'll need to ask for a refund.

If you paid VFS Global directly before you attended the visa application centre, you can request a refund in your VFS Global account. Select 'services' then 'cancel services'.

If you paid TLScontact at your appointment, email the priority services refund requests team and explain why you think you should get a refund.

Priority services refund requests team
ukvi.visa.pvspv.customerrefundrequests@homeoffice.gov.uk

## When you'll get your refund

Your refund will be paid into the same bank account you used to pay the priority service fee.

It can take up to 28 days to get your refund.

### If you have not received your refund within 28 days

Contact UK Visas and Immigration for help if you do not get your refund within 28 days of either:

- getting your refund confirmation email

- cancelling your application - if you did not get a refund confirmation email
